questions.text: In the LDA generative model, the document-topic distribution θ_d is drawn from:
options: A Gaussian distribution with mean equal to the number of topics
A Dirichlet distribution with concentration parameter α
A uniform distribution over all possible topic combinations
A multinomial distribution over the words in the vocabulary
questions.explanation: θ_d ~ Dir(α) is the document-topic distribution — a probability vector over K topics. The Dirichlet is the natural prior for a multinomial proportion. The α parameter controls how concentrated or diffuse this distribution is across topics.

questions.text: A Dirichlet concentration parameter α = 0.1 (very small) implies:
options: Each document covers all topics roughly equally
Each document is dominated by one or two topics (sparse topic mixtures)
All topics have equal probability in every document
The model has only 0.1 topics on average per document
questions.explanation: Low α concentrates the Dirichlet distribution near the corners of the simplex, where most of the probability mass is on one or two topics. High α concentrates near the centre (equal proportions). For topic modelling, α < 1 is typical to encourage specialised, interpretable topics.

questions.text: The β (beta) matrix from LDA has dimensions K × V (topics × vocabulary). What does entry β[k, w] represent?
options: The probability that topic k was generated by document w
The probability of observing word w in topic k
The TF-IDF score of word w in topic k
The number of times word w appears in documents assigned to topic k
questions.explanation: β[k, w] = P(word w | topic k). It is the word-topic distribution — the probability that if you were writing a document about topic k, you would use word w at any given word position. High-β words characterise the topic.

questions.text: Perplexity in LDA is used to:
options: Measure how coherent each topic is based on the top words
Evaluate how well the model predicts held-out text — lower is better
Count the number of unique words assigned to each topic
Assess whether the Gibbs sampler has converged
questions.explanation: Perplexity = exp(−(1/N)Σlog P(word)). It measures the model's surprise at new text: a well-fit model predicts held-out words with higher probability, giving lower perplexity. It is used to compare models with different K values, choosing K at the elbow of the perplexity curve.

questions.text: LDA is a supervised learning method that requires labelled complaint categories to discover topics.
questions.explanation: LDA is unsupervised. It discovers latent topics from the word co-occurrence patterns without any labels. This is its key advantage: it can reveal topics you did not know existed. Supervised counterparts (e.g., supervised LDA) exist but are a different model.

questions.text: You fit LDA with K = 5 on insurance complaints and find that Topic 3 has top words: 'claim', 'pending', 'submitted', 'documents', 'months'. Which business action is most directly supported by this topic?
options: Redesign the mobile app to reduce complaints about poor UX
Improve the claims processing pipeline to reduce resolution times
Adjust premium pricing for high-risk policyholders
Redesign the dental and vision cover product bundle
questions.explanation: The words 'pending', 'months', 'submitted', and 'documents' point to delays in claims processing — the claim has been received but not resolved. This directly suggests improving the internal claims processing pipeline: faster document verification, automated status updates, and escalation triggers for long-pending claims.
